observed_while_building: The exit pair's asymmetry is what makes it checkable, and only one half of a swap is caught. `shape_satisfies` deliberately treats a ONE-dimensional contract as satisfied by any shape holding the same values in the same order, so a `[1, hidden]` tensor stored under the norm's name does satisfy `[hidden]`; the projection's two-dimensional contract has no such latitude and refuses a `[hidden]` tensor. Had the reference stored the projection as a bare vector — the same numbers — a swapped pair would satisfy both contracts and no geometry test could exist. Recorded in the test rather than asserted around: geometry separates these two operands, and nothing in this transition proves an executor would read them in the right order. That is the oracle's job.

The canonical cache answers the control question on the OBJECTS plane, not only on the findings plane, and it had to. Searching every plan's `graph.objects[].source_bindings[].tensor_prefix` found the swept norm sitting inside `target.final_norm` on the one row that has it, which is the reconnaissance's 'silent one' visible as data.

FALSIFIED_decision_5_one_candidate.what_the_source_says: at layer 0 the mlp-site reduction runs over TWO candidates. The order in `_forward_attn_residual` is: attention-site reduce (guarded on a non-empty set, so skipped at layer 0), THEN the boundary snapshot appends the entering state, THEN the sublayer, THEN the mlp-site reduce. Layer 0 is a boundary (`0 % B == 0`), so by the time the mlp site runs the set already holds one snapshot and the candidates are {snapshot, prefix} = 2.
FALSIFIED_decision_5_one_candidate.and_it_never_occurs: no site in this schedule EVER reduces over one candidate. The set starts empty (`new_zeros(tokens, 0, hidden)`), layer 0 always snapshots, and the set only grows — so the empty-set case exists at exactly one site in the whole stack, layer 0's ATTENTION site, where the reference's guard skips the reduction rather than running it over one candidate. Measured in the fixture: candidate counts are 2, 2, 2, 2/3, 3, 3, 3/4 and 4 at the exit; the minimum anywhere is 2.

observed_while_building: **The first draft of this oracle rejected nothing, and looked like it was passing.** Its score pairs were drawn at the layer scales (up to 4.0), so `score = sum_h k_h * (norm_h * proj_h)` over an RMS-normalised `k` produced probabilities of `[1.0, 4.2e-11]` — a softmax saturated to one-hot. On a saturated distribution every candidate-set control is INVISIBLE: a candidate carrying 4e-11 of the mass can be added, removed or duplicated without moving the mix, so `attn_site_over_new_snapshots` measured exactly 0.0 while the mutation was demonstrably taking effect (its witness showed 2 candidates where the reference had none, and 3 where the reference had 2). The structure changed and the numbers did not. Fixed by drawing the score pair small (0.15) and the branch weights at the layer scales — two roles that the first draft had conflated: the score pair decides whether the softmax can DISCRIMINATE, the branch weights decide whether the candidates are worth discriminating between.

**The fixture now asserts its own ability to see.** `_verify` checks, FIRST, that no site's probability distribution is flatter than 5e-3 or more peaked than 0.98, and the measured band (0.112 .. 0.756) ships in the JSON. Without that assertion a future regeneration could re-saturate the fixture and every control would go quiet without a single test failing — the instrument would keep reporting success while measuring nothing. This is the [[feedback_verification_needs_verification]] shape applied to an oracle: if a check returns the answer you wanted, prove it could have returned the other.

Two of the ten controls are exactly 0.0 and both are mathematically necessary rather than fixture artefacts — softmax over one candidate is the identity, and the mlp site's guard never fires. They are reported as `numerically_inert` in the JSON with the reason, so the traversal transition can see up front that two of its six properties need a WITNESS comparison and cannot be checked by output parity alone.
oracle.what_the_oracle_does_not_claim: It is a transcription, and a transcription can be faithful to the wrong file or faithful in the wrong dtype. It runs the reference's own f32-internal reduction on f32 inputs; a bf16 checkpoint would enter `_apply_attn_res` at bf16 and leave it cast back, which this fixture does not exercise. It uses a stand-in sublayer (pre-norm, linear, tanh), so nothing here checks KDA, MLA or MoE. And no Rust reads it yet: this boundary adds an instrument, not a capability.
